provenance: Authored by reading eval/corpus/ directly, BEFORE any retrieval implementation existed. No retrieval output influenced any entry.
notes: answer_units are file paths. evidence_must_contain is a substring that the cited evidence span must include, checked verbatim against the source.

queries.query: PAYMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
queries.expected: Defined in orderflow/config.py with value 30.

queries.query: SETTLEMENT_BATCH_SIZE
queries.expected: Defined in orderflow/config.py with value 500.

queries.query: GatewayError
queries.expected: Exception class defined in orderflow/gateway.py.

queries.query: payment gateway deadline
queries.expected: 30 seconds, per ADR-007 and config.

queries.query: append-only ledger money movements
queries.expected: The Ledger class records money movements append-only.

queries.query: at what point do we stop waiting for a stalled purchase
queries.expected: After 30 seconds; PAYMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS in config.py, rationale in ADR-007.

queries.query: why do shoppers walk away from a slow checkout
queries.expected: Shoppers abandon a transaction pending about half a minute; documented in the abandonment study and cited as ADR-007 rationale.

queries.query: how is the bookkeeping of funds handled
queries.expected: An append-only ledger records every money movement.

queries.query: which components ultimately depend on the payment timeout configuration
queries.expected: gateway.CardGateway imports it directly; payments.PaymentProcessor uses CardGateway; api.post_charge builds the processor.

queries.query: what does post_charge end up calling
queries.expected: post_charge -> build_processor -> PaymentProcessor.charge -> CardGateway.authorize/capture -> Ledger.record.

queries.query: what is the gateway deadline and why was that value chosen
queries.expected: 30 seconds (config.py); chosen because p99 was 18s and shoppers abandon beyond ~30s (ADR-007).

queries.query: which API endpoint triggers a card authorization
queries.expected: POST /charge maps to post_charge, which authorizes via the gateway.

queries.query: Processor
queries.expected: TWO distinct classes: payments.PaymentProcessor and reporting.Processor. They are unrelated and must not be merged.

queries.query: record
queries.expected: Ledger.record is the method; 'record' also appears as prose in docs. The code symbol is in ledger.py.

queries.query: what is the Kafka topic used for order events
queries.expected: UNSUPPORTED: the corpus contains no Kafka, no message broker and no event topics.

queries.query: which GDPR data retention period applies to cardholder names
queries.expected: UNSUPPORTED: the corpus says nothing about GDPR or data retention.

queries.query: what is the gateway timeout value
queries.expected: CONFLICT: config.py, ADR-007, architecture.md and settings.json all say 30 seconds; runbook.md says 60 seconds and is self-described as last reviewed in 2024. Both positions must be returned; the conflict must not be silently resolved.

queries.query: what is the 99th percentile card network response time
queries.expected: 18 seconds under peak traffic, stated in ADR-007 rationale.

queries.query: what is the settlement batch size
queries.expected: 500, defined in config.py and used by Ledger.settle.

queries.query: what does PaymentProcessor.charge call
queries.expected: self.gateway.authorize, self.gateway.capture, self.ledger.record.

queries.query: which module imports SETTLEMENT_BATCH_SIZE
queries.expected: orderflow/ledger.py imports it from orderflow.config.

queries.query: processor deadline
queries.expected: The deadline belongs to the gateway (CardGateway.deadline), not to reporting.Processor. A retriever matching 'processor' lexically will surface reporting.py, which is wrong.

queries.query: what code is affected by changing the abandonment threshold
queries.expected: config.py defines it; gateway.py consumes it; payments.py and api.py depend transitively. 'abandonment threshold' appears in none of those files.
